exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I'm watching my sodium intake. Which brand or product should I choose, and why?
reviewed_answer:
My top recommendation is Friendship Dairies No Salt Added 1% Cottage Cheese. It provides just 45 mg of sodium per ½-cup serving while delivering 16 g of protein—an excellent combination if you're trying to reduce sodium without sacrificing nutrition.

What I would choose

First choice: Friendship Dairies No Salt Added. Lowest sodium among these options, high protein, and a relatively simple ingredient list.

Excellent alternative: Hood No Salt Added Low Fat. Only 15 mg more sodium per serving, with a creamy formulation that may appeal if you find unsalted cottage cheese bland.

If neither is available: Prairie Farms Low Sodium or Breakstone's Low Sodium can still reduce sodium compared with many regular versions, but they're substantially saltier than the no-salt-added choices.

When shopping, look for “No Salt Added” rather than just “Low Fat.” Reducing fat doesn't necessarily reduce sodium. Also remember that “no salt added” doesn't mean sodium-free; milk naturally contains some sodium.

For most U.S. adults, the general recommended sodium limit is less than 2,300 mg daily, although your clinician may recommend a lower target.

Bottom line: Buy Friendship Dairies No Salt Added 1% if you can find it. Hood No Salt Added is a very close second. Both let you enjoy high-protein cottage cheese while using only a small portion of your daily sodium allowance.
